I've farmed this land my whole life. My father farmed it before me. I know Quzhou's soil — it's heavy clay-loam, holds water decent, but needs good inputs to push yields. Two people in the house means I do most of the work myself, so I keep things manageable.

In a wheat-maize rotation, all 25.1 mu runs both crops — wheat over winter, maize over summer. That's how we've always done it here and it works. I'm not going to split the land differently.

**Wheat**: I'll use the Jimai improved variety — it's reliable here, local seed dealers stock it, and I've used similar lines for years. I'll plough before planting in early October. I apply compound fertilizer (磷酸二铵) as base plus urea at jointing. Four irrigations: one before sowing to get soil moisture right, one in December to help overwintering, one at jointing in April, one at grain-fill. Three pesticide passes — herbicide in late autumn when weeds are small, fungicide for powdery mildew around April, and something for aphids close to harvest. I expect around 480 jin... 480 kg per mu if the season is decent.

**Maize**: After wheat harvest in June, I'll rotary-till quickly — no time to plough, need to get the maize in fast. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, it's proven here for decades. Summer rains usually help, so only two irrigations — one at planting if soil is dry, one if there's a drought around tasseling. Two pesticide applications: pre-emergence herbicide and one for corn borer. Fertilizer goes in as base compound plus urea topdress at V6-V8. I expect 550 kg per mu in a normal year.
